body.statement:
For each fixed \(P_0\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal F_s)\), there are positive constants \(c_1(P_0),c_2(P_0),C_{P_0},\zeta_0(P_0)\) and a sample threshold, all allowed to depend on the \(C^s\), ellipticity, lift-branch, and cut-locus margins of \(P_0\), such that, for all sufficiently small \(\varepsilon\),
\[
c_1(P_0)\log(1/\varepsilon)
\leq \lVert\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\rVert_{L^2(P_{0g_\star})}^2
\leq c_2(P_0)\log(1/\varepsilon),
\qquad
\lVert f_{0g_\star}\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\rVert_{C^s}
\leq C_{P_0}\varepsilon^{-s-1}.
\]
For every fixed \(0<\zeta\leq\zeta_0(P_0)\) satisfying \(C_{P_0}\zeta^2\leq\kappa\), the laws in def:green-local-alternatives satisfy, for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
P_{n,+},P_{n,-}\in\mathcal F_s\cap\mathcal N_n(P_0,\kappa),
\]
\[
\operatorname{Hel}^2\!\left(
\bigotimes_{g\in\mathcal G}P_{n,+,g}^{\otimes n_g},
\bigotimes_{g\in\mathcal G}P_{n,-,g}^{\otimes n_g}
\right)
\leq C_{P_0}\zeta^2\leq\frac12,
\]
and
\[
\left|\upsilon^{\mathsf T}\{\tau(P_{n,+})-\tau(P_{n,-})\}_1\right|
\geq c_1(P_0)\zeta\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}{n}}.
\]
Here \(\eta<1/[2(s+1)]\) makes the \(C^s\) perturbation tend to zero.  For either sign, causal-class membership is witnessed by \(h_0=\operatorname{id}\), \(\nu_C=P_{n,\pm,C0}\), \(\nu_T=P_{n,\pm,T0}\), \(h_1=p\), and \(h_{1\star}=T^{-1}\circ p\).  Moreover,
\[
\lVert a_p(P_{n,\pm})-a_p(P_0)\rVert
+\lVert a_T(P_{n,\pm})-a_T(P_0)\rVert=O_{P_0,\zeta}(n^{-1/2}),
\]
so the selected-lift harmonic changes are negligible relative to \(\sqrt{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)/n}\).
body.justification: The corrected harmonic scores are bounded and therefore do not alter the annular logarithmic leading separation.
body.gap: The final fixed-center path remainder must be reattached to the corrected derivative after the formal definition change.
body.consumer: Completion would certify the local lower-bound alternatives.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(P_0\in\operatorname{int}(\mathcal F_s)\) and put
\(\Theta(P)=\upsilon^{\mathsf T}\tau_1(P)\).  All constants in this proof may depend on the fixed center and its strict margins.  By thm:nested-derivative, the cell-
\(g_\star\) derivative of \(\Theta\) is the leading outer Green functional with representer \(\varphi_{g_\star}\), plus order-minus-two and weighted-Hodge harmonic functionals having bounded \(L^2(P_{0g_\star})\) representers.

Let \(x_\star\) be the unique pullback of \(y_1\) to the \(g_\star\)-cell coordinates.  The parametrix construction in lem:uniform-critical-estimates and invertibility of all coordinate pullbacks give, on a fixed ball about \(x_\star\),
\[
 \varphi_{g_\star}(x)=
 \frac{b_{g_\star}^{\mathsf T}(x-x_\star)}
 {|E_{g_\star}(x-x_\star)|^2}+r_{g_\star}(x),
 \qquad b_{g_\star}\neq0,
\tag{1}
\]
where \(E_{g_\star}\) is invertible and, for \(0\leq m\leq s\),
\[
 |\nabla^m r_{g_\star}(x)|
 \leq C|x-x_\star|^{-m}\{1+|\log|x-x_\star||\}.
\tag{2}
\]
The numerator in (1) is nonzero because \(\upsilon\neq0\), the pullbacks have full rank, the outer Green matrix is positive definite, and the cell multiplier is either \(1\) or the positive number \(\alpha(y_1)\).

An anisotropic polar change of variables in (1), followed by (2), gives a number \(a_{g_\star}(P_0)>0\) such that
\[
 \int\chi_\varepsilon^2\varphi_{g_\star}^2\,dP_{0g_\star}
 =a_{g_\star}(P_0)\log(1/\varepsilon)+O_{P_0}(1).
\tag{3}
\]
The centering integral is bounded because \(1/|x-x_\star|\) is locally integrable in two dimensions.  Hence centering changes (3) by only \(O_{P_0}(1)\), proving the asserted two-sided logarithmic bounds.  Leibniz's rule, (1)--(2), and the transition bounds defining \(\chi_\varepsilon\) also give, separately for every \(0\leq m\leq s\),
\[
 \lVert\nabla^m(\chi_\varepsilon\varphi_{g_\star})\rVert_\infty
 \leq C_{P_0}\varepsilon^{-m-1}.
\tag{4}
\]
After centering and multiplication by \(f_{0g_\star}\), the case \(m=s\) proves the claimed \(C^s\) envelope.

Set
\[
 u_n=\frac{\zeta\ell_{\varepsilon_n,g_\star}}
 {\sqrt n\,\lVert\ell_{\varepsilon_n,g_\star}\rVert_{L^2(P_{0g_\star})}}.
\tag{5}
\]
It is centered under \(P_{0g_\star}\), so both alternatives have mass one.  Equations (3)--(5) imply
\[
 \lVert u_n\rVert_2=\zeta n^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 \lVert f_{0g_\star}u_n\rVert_{C^s}
 \leq\frac{C_{P_0}\zeta\varepsilon_n^{-s-1}}
 {\sqrt{n\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}}=o(1),
\tag{6}
\]
because \(\eta(s+1)<1/2\).  The case \(m=0\) in (4) gives \(\lVert u_n\rVert_\infty=o(1)\); therefore both densities are positive for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The strict interior margins of \(P_0\), continuity of the two augmented transport systems, and (6) retain density bounds, ellipticity, and the lift and cut-locus margins.

Membership in the causal class is also explicit.  For either sign let \(p\) and \(T\) be the transports generated by the perturbed four laws and set
\[
 h_0=\operatorname{id},\qquad \nu_C=P_{C0},\qquad
 \nu_T=P_{T0},\qquad h_1=p,qquad h_{1\star}=T^{-1}\circ p.
\tag{7}
\]
Then \(h_1\#\nu_C=P_{C1}\),
\(h_{1\star}\#\nu_T=T^{-1}\#(p\#P_{T0})=P_{T1}\), and
\(h_1\circ h_0^{-1}=p\), \(h_1\circ h_{1\star}^{-1}=T\).  The last two graphs are \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclically monotone by their defining optimality.  Thus (7) verifies ass:cic-identification and proves membership in \(\mathcal F_s\).

For \(|v|\leq1/2\), \((\sqrt{1+v}-1)^2\leq v^2\).  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Hel}^2(P_{n,\pm,g_\star},P_{0g_\star})
 \leq\int u_n^2\,dP_{0g_\star}=\frac{\zeta^2}{n}.
\tag{8}
\]
All other cells are unchanged.  This proves neighborhood membership after choosing \(C_{P_0}\zeta^2\leq\kappa\).  Similarly,
\[
 \operatorname{Hel}^2(P_{n,+,g_\star},P_{n,-,g_\star})
 \leq C\zeta^2/n.
\tag{9}
\]
Since squared Hellinger distance of product laws is at most the sum of the component squared distances and \(n_{g_\star}=n\), (9) gives the claimed product bound; decreasing \(\zeta_0(P_0)\) makes it at most \(1/2\).

We prove separation with the corrected harmonic terms retained.  Centering \(\varphi_{g_\star}\) does not change its action on density tangents, and (1)--(3) give
\[
 \int\varphi_{g_\star}\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\,dP_{0g_\star}
 =\lVert\ell_{\varepsilon,g_\star}\rVert_2^2+O_{P_0}(1).
\tag{10}
\]
Every order-minus-two or harmonic representer is bounded in \(L^2\), so its pairing with \(u_n\) is \(O_{P_0,\zeta}(n^{-1/2})\).  Hence
\[
 D\Theta_{P_0}[f_{0g_\star}u_n]
 =\frac{\zeta}{\sqrt n}\lVert\ell_{\varepsilon_n,g_\star}\rVert_2
 +O_{P_0,\zeta}(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{11}
\]
Use the mixed Fr\'echet remainder (34) from thm:nested-derivative separately for the positive and negative endpoints.  The order-specific bound (4), rather than its crude \(C^s\) consequence, gives
\[
 U_1\leq\frac{C\zeta\varepsilon_n^{-2}}
 {\sqrt{n\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}},
 \qquad
 U_0\leq\frac{C\zeta\varepsilon_n^{-1}}
 {\sqrt{n\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}}.
\tag{12}
\]
Thus each endpoint remainder is at most
\[
 CU_1U_0\leq
 \frac{C\zeta^2\varepsilon_n^{-3}}{n\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}
 =o\!\left(\zeta\sqrt{\frac{\log(1/\varepsilon_n)}n}\right),
\tag{13}
\]
because \(\eta<1/[2(s+1)]\leq1/18<1/6\).  Equations (3), (11), and (13) prove the displayed two-sided separation after decreasing \(c_1(P_0)\).

Finally, the bounded Riesz scores for \(b_p\) and \(b_T\) in thm:nested-derivative, positivity along both line segments, and (5) yield by integration
\[
 \lVert a_p(P_{n,\pm})-a_p(P_0)\rVert+
 \lVert a_T(P_{n,\pm})-a_T(P_0)\rVert
 \leq C_{P_0}\lVert u_n\rVert_2
 =O_{P_0,\zeta}(n^{-1/2}).
\tag{14}
\]
This is negligible relative to the logarithmic separation and completes the proof.
